title: Anchoring trust in money: innovation beyond stablecoins (Annual Economic Report 2026, Chapter III)
date_evidence: Page dateline: 23 June 2026 (chapter 'Anchoring trust in money: innovation beyond stablecoins', BIS Annual Economic Report 2026)
key_claim: Stablecoins display some of tokenisation's potential but current designs fall short on foundational properties of money, in particular singleness, elasticity, interoperability and integrity, and threaten financial integrity; a unified ledger integrating tokenised central bank reserves, tokenised commercial bank money and other appropriately supervised private monies and tokenised assets could realise the benefits of tokenisation while maintaining trust, with Project Agorá, a public-private partnership of eight central banks and over 40 regulated institutions, showcased as evidence the model can work; advancing the next-generation monetary system requires tackling stablecoin weaknesses and bringing tokenisation into the two-tier system.
frame_summary: The BIS argues the future monetary system should be built on tokenised, central-bank-anchored unified ledgers inside the two-tier banking system, and that stablecoins as currently designed cannot be its foundation.
notes: Doctrinal anchor for the counter-system framing; chapter pre-released 23 June 2026 ahead of the BIS annual general meeting.

title: Project Agorá shows how tokenisation can improve wholesale cross-border payments; work will advance to real-value testing (press release)
key_claim: The Agorá prototype demonstrated atomic settlement of wholesale cross-border transactions using tokenised central bank reserves and tokenised commercial bank deposits, achievable securely and with finality across currencies and jurisdictions; legal analysis finds settlement finality achievable in all seven participating jurisdictions; the project, involving the Bank of England, the New York Fed, the Bank of France, the Bank of Japan, the Bank of Korea, the Bank of Mexico, the Swiss National Bank and more than 40 private financial institutions, will advance to real-value transactions, with the Bank of Canada joining and an enhanced private-sector role expected.
frame_summary: The BIS and participating central banks present tokenised two-tier money as demonstrated engineering ready for real-value testing, positioning the public-private unified platform as the credible upgrade path for cross-border payments.
notes: Milestone press release accompanying the Agorá findings report (othp110).

title: Tokenized Finance (IMF Notes No. 26/01)
date_evidence: Tokenized Finance; IMF Notes No. 26/01; April 2026 (IMF publication listing); elibrary page: 'Tokenized Finance in: IMF Notes Volume 2026 Issue 001 (2026)'
key_claim: Tokenization's core effect on banking is not disintermediation but a reconfiguration of the ways banks manage trust, liquidity and risk as money creation, credit intermediation and payments migrate onto programmable shared ledgers; the settlement asset is the cornerstone of any financial system, with central bank money anchoring convertibility and the singleness of money, and tokenization reopens this question; atomic settlement and transparency reduce some traditional risks while speed and automation mean stress events unfold faster, so stability requires tokenized arrangements anchored in safe settlement assets, legally recognized finality and robust governance.
frame_summary: The IMF frames tokenisation as a reorganisation of the existing two-tier system around the choice of settlement asset, arguing stability depends on anchoring tokenised money in central bank money rather than on whichever token scales fastest.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6 month band): canonical multilateral framing of tokenised finance published April 2026; date carried by the IMF's own publication listing (insea2026001).

title: JPMorgan, Bank of America, Citi to start blockchain offensive with shared tokenized network
key_claim: America's biggest banks, including JPMorgan, Citi and Bank of America, plan a shared tokenized deposit network by the first half of 2027, operated by The Clearing House, according to the Wall Street Journal; the system converts customer deposits into blockchain tokens that move quickly around the clock while keeping funds inside the regulated banking system; the Clarity Act advancing through Congress could allow stablecoins to pay returns to holders, threatening deposit flight to crypto wallets; a blockchain vendor has not yet been selected.
frame_summary: CoinDesk reads the Clearing House network as Wall Street's coordinated defensive move: banks giving deposits crypto-like capabilities precisely because yield-bearing stablecoins threaten their funding base.
notes: Carries the underlying Wall Street Journal reporting; quantifies the launch window (H1 2027).

title: US banks tap The Clearing House for tokenized deposit network
key_claim: The Clearing House is the logical operator as it already runs CHIPS, EPN and RTP; it is owned by 21 banks including JP Morgan, Citi, Bank of America and Wells Fargo, plus multinational shareholders TD, BMO, Barclays, Deutsche Bank, HSBC and Santander, giving future cross-border potential; most large US banks' existing tokenized deposits work only for their own customers, whereas the TCH solution will support interbank payments; multiple other US tokenized deposit networks are emerging for mid-size and community banks, including the Cari Network and the Hazel Network founded by Vantage and Custodia.
frame_summary: The specialist trade press frames the announcement as the interbank layer arriving on top of single-bank token silos, while noting a proliferating field of parallel bank networks whose access models remain undecided.
notes: Enterprise-blockchain trade press; adds ownership detail and the parallel-network landscape used in the counter-argument.

title: BIS says stablecoins fall short as money, warns of emerging-market risks in annual report
key_claim: The BIS Annual Economic Report 2026 judges stablecoins against singleness, elasticity, interoperability and integrity and finds current designs come up short, arguing the tokens resemble exchange-traded fund shares more than a means of payment; the BIS put total stablecoin market value at roughly $320 billion at the end of May, with more than 99% of fiat-backed supply pegged to the US dollar; its US-calibrated model finds the net output effect of stablecoins slightly negative over the medium term even at $1 trillion, $2 trillion and $3 trillion in market value, as higher bank funding costs and weaker lending outweigh fiscal room; the report warns of stablecoin dollarization in emerging economies and pitches a tokenized unified ledger anchored in central bank money.
frame_summary: Crypto-native media relays the BIS verdict largely on the BIS's own terms while supplying the market data showing how small stablecoins remain next to the banking system they are said to threaten.
notes: Quantification carrier for the $320 billion supply figure, the >99% dollar peg share and the $1-3 trillion adoption model.

title: Stablecoins, tokenized deposits and CBDCs are scaling - but trust still has to cross systems
key_claim: Stablecoins, tokenized deposits, CBDC experiments and bank-led DLT systems are scaling in parallel rather than converging into one architecture, with bank and market-infrastructure systems such as JPMorgan's Kinexys, HSBC's tokenized deposits, Fnality's wholesale settlement system and Project Agorá moving from pilots toward early commercialization; the unresolved problem is not payment speed but cross-system trust, compliance verification and settlement recognition across sovereign, regulated and institutionally different systems.
frame_summary: A vendor-commissioned essay argues fragmentation across parallel settlement systems is the durable condition and that interoperability requires verifiable cross-system evidence rather than convergence on one ledger.
notes: Sponsored content used only as directional corroboration of the interoperability/fragmentation counter-thread.
